blocks.h2: How Your New Gas Line Goes In

steps.body: For the new appliance and everything already on it.
Through basements and joists where possible.

blocks.intro: Remodels in older homes often mean new gas work.

items.body: Moving the range means a new branch.
Grills and fire pits on the patio.

blocks.body: A six-burner range with a griddle can use far more gas than the stove it replaces. In older Evanston homes, the original line to the kitchen is often too small to feed it properly, so burners run weak when the oven and furnace are on too. We add up the total load, check the pipe size back to the meter and upsize the line where needed. Then the new range gets the flame it was designed for.

blocks.h2: What Affects the Price of a New Gas Line
blocks.body: Length and route matter most. A short branch in an open basement is simple. A line through finished space, to an upper floor or out to the patio takes more work. If the existing pipe is too small for the new load, part of it may need upsizing. We plan the route and quote one flat price.

blocks.h2: Gas Line Installation Questions From Evanston Homeowners

items.q: Can my existing gas line handle a new range?
items.answer: We calculate the load and check the pipe before connecting.
Yes, where the city requires one.

items.q: Can you run gas to the patio?
items.answer: Yes, with a protected line and a shutoff.

items.q: Can you switch my dryer from electric to gas?
items.preview: Yes, if a line can reach it.
items.answer: Yes. We run a branch line and add a shutoff at the dryer.

items.q: Can you move my range to an island?
items.answer: Usually, by running the line under the floor. We'll check the route first.

items.q: Can one line feed a grill and a fire pit?
items.answer: Yes, if it's sized for both, with a shutoff at each.

items.q: How much does gas line installation cost in Evanston?
items.preview: It depends on the run. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on the length of the run, the appliance and the route. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
